insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

great.name: Hospice Care benefit (indemnity) available with 12-month waiting
great.quote: Hospice Care : Payable up to 20% of sum insured at network providers on indemnity basis, payable once in life time. Available after a waiting period of 12 months from the policy inception.
great.explanation: Hospice care is covered (up to 20% of Sum Insured, once in lifetime) after 12 months waiting, which is relatively favorable for a specialized cancer-focused benefit.

great.name: All day care procedures covered
great.quote: g) All day care procedures are covered.
great.explanation: Day care treatments (procedures that do not require 24-hour hospitalization) are covered.

good.name: Room rent (default): Single Standard A/c room
good.quote: a) Room (Single Standard A/c), Boarding, Nursing expenses as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home.
good.explanation: Room eligibility is Single Standard AC room, which is standard in many plans (not 'any room').

good.name: Initial waiting period: 30 days (except accidents)
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the ﬁrst policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Standard initial waiting period for illnesses; accidents are typically exempt.

good.name: Specific illness / procedure waiting period: 24 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of the listed Conditions, surgeries/treatments shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with us.
good.reference: Exclusions, Code Excl 02 (Specified disease / procedure waiting period)
good.explanation: A standard 24-month waiting applies to listed specific diseases/procedures.

good.name: PED waiting period: 30 months
good.quote: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry 30 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the ﬁrst policy with insurer.
good.reference: PED exclusion text shown in document (under exclusions section content near modern treatment table)
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered after 30 months of continuous coverage. This is within the 'good' range (≤48 months).

good.name: Co-pay: 10% for entry age 61+
good.quote: Copayment : This policy is subject to co-payment of 10% of each and every claim amount for fresh as well as renewal policies for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
good.explanation: Industry-standard senior-age co-pay: if entry age is 61+, you pay 10% of every claim.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization: 30 days
good.quote: e) Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
good.explanation: Covers eligible medical expenses for 30 days before hospitalization (standard).

good.name: Post-hospitalization: 60 days (with 2% of SI cap per hospitalization)
good.quote: f) Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital. The amount payable shall be up to 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization.
good.explanation: Covers eligible expenses for 60 days post discharge, but payout is capped at 2% of Basic SI per hospitalization.

good.name: NCB / Cumulative Bonus: 5% per claim-free year up to 50% (reduces on claims)
good.quote: Cumulative bonus calculated at 5% of basic sum insured for each claim free year subject to a maximum of 50% of the basic sum insured... In the event of a claim... such cumulative bonus so granted will be reduced at the same rate at which it has accrued
good.explanation: NCB grows up to 50% but is reduced when claims occur (not a protected/non-resetting bonus).

good.name: AYUSH inpatient hospitalization covered (Yoga/Naturopathy with prior approval)
good.quote: AYUSH Treatment: Medical expenses for Inpatient Hospitalization incurred on treatment under Ayurveda, Unani, Sidha and Homeopathy systems of medicines in a AYUSH Hospital is payable up to the sum insured. Note : Claims under Yoga and Naturopathy system of treatment will be payable subject to prior approval from the company.
good.explanation: AYUSH inpatient treatments are covered up to SI; Yoga/Naturopathy needs prior approval.

good.name: Optional add-on: Lump-sum cover for cancer recurrence/metastasis/second malignancy (30-month waiting)
good.quote: Section  II  Lumpsum Cover for Cancer (Optional Cover Available only if speciﬁcally opted on payment of additional premium and shown in the policy schedule)... A waiting period of 30 months is applicable for this lump-sum beneﬁt cover
good.explanation: Optional paid cover: pays a lump-sum for recurrence/metastasis/second unrelated malignancy after 30 months; it is in addition to the indemnity SI.

bad.name: Modern treatments covered with sub-limits (not at actuals)
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern treatment... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below.
bad.explanation: Modern treatments have explicit caps/sub-limits, which can increase out-of-pocket costs for advanced procedures.

bad.name: Cataract sub-limits
bad.quote: Cataract treatment: The company will pay the expenses incurred for treatment of cataract up to the limits mentioned below; ... 5,00,000/- 30,000/- per eye per person and not exceeding 40,000/- per person per policy period ... 7,50,000/- and 10,00,000/- 40,000/- per eye per person and not exceeding 60,000/- per person per policy period
bad.reference: Section I (h) and cataract limit table
bad.explanation: Cataract has defined monetary caps, which can be restrictive depending on hospital/doctor charges.

bad.name: Room-category linked proportionate deductions apply (because room is capped to Single Standard AC)
bad.quote: Hospitalisation expenses which vary based on the room occupied by the insured person will be considered in proportion to the room category stated in the policy schedule or actuals whichever is less.
bad.reference: Section I (a) Note; also aligns with 'Associated Medical Expenses' definition
bad.explanation: If you take a higher room category than eligible, proportionate deductions can reduce payouts for certain associated medical expenses (beyond just the room rent difference).

bad.name: Post-hospitalization payout capped at 2% of Basic SI per hospitalization
bad.quote: The amount payable shall be up to 2% of the basic sum insured per hospitalization.
bad.explanation: Even though 60 days is covered, the payable amount is capped at 2% of SI per hospitalization, which can be limiting for expensive medicines/follow-ups.

bad.name: No restore benefit mentioned (mandatory feature) — Sum Insured not replenished after claim
bad.quote: Not mentioned in the provided policy wording text.
bad.reference: Document review: no restore/reinstatement/recharge clause found in provided pages
bad.explanation: No restore/recharge benefit is stated here. After a claim exhausts the Sum Insured, it may not be replenished for the same policy year.

bad.name: Consumables not explicitly covered (mandatory feature) — likely out-of-pocket
bad.quote: Not mentioned in the coverage as 'consumables covered' or any consumables add-on/benefit.
bad.reference: Section I coverage list (a)-(p) does not state consumables are covered separately
bad.explanation: The policy does not explicitly state that consumables (gloves, syringes, PPE, etc.) are covered as a separate benefit. If hospitals bill these separately, they may be payable by you unless included under other admissible heads as per insurer rules.

unclear.name: Co-pay for ages below 61: not explicitly stated (mandatory reporting)
unclear.quote: Copayment : This policy is subject to co-payment of 10%... for insured persons whose age at the time of entry is 61 years and above.
unclear.explanation: The document clearly states co-pay for entry age 61+, but it does not explicitly say 'no co-pay' for others. Confirm from the policy schedule/insurer whether co-pay is 0% for entry age <61.

unclear.name: NCB treatment on claims: reduction mechanism described but 'reset to zero' not explicitly stated
unclear.quote: In the event of a claim resulting in... the cumulative bonus so granted will be reduced at the same rate at which it has accrued... Full utilization of Basic Sum Insured and full utilization of cumulative bonus accrued, the cumulative bonus on renewal will be “nil”
unclear.explanation: The wording explains reductions and can lead to 'nil' bonus depending on utilization, but the exact behavior for small claims (e.g., whether bonus reduces proportionately every time and how it is computed) should be confirmed via examples/insurer.

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
